 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 30(1) of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (hereinafter referred to as 'WC Act' for short), challenging the judgment and award passed in case No.WCA/NF.No.91/2002 dated 10.01.2012 by the Labour Officer and Commissioner for the Workmen Compensation, Division - 2, Chikmagalur, questioning the liability fixed on the owner of the Tractor-Trailer and also for enhancement of compensation.
2.

The undisputed facts are that on 25.08.2001, the claimant loaded the materials to the Tractor-Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-18-3641-3642, which belongs to respondent No.1 and when he was proceeding on Kadur - Shringeri road, near Kuduvalli Village, the said Tractor-Trailer has turned turtle and due to which, the claimant had sustained grievous injuries.
NC: 2023:KHC:24855
Therefore, the claimant has filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that there is no violation of condition in insurance policy.
But learned Commissioner has wrongly assigned the reason and fastened liability on the owner.
Hence, prays for modification of the judgment.
He also submitted that the monthly wage held by the Commissioner is meager and has taken lesser percentage of disability.

Hence,
prays for modification of judgment and enhancement of compensation.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 justified the judgment and award passed by the learned Commissioner.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.

Sri Nagaraj vs Ninge Gowda on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171243086/
2 6.

In the present case, learned Commissioner has fastened the liability on the owner of the Tractor-Trailer on the ground that insurance policy was issued towards agriculture purpose but the owner has given the said Tractor-Trailer on contract basis to one K.S.Raju and the said contractor has NC: 2023:KHC:24855 utilized the said Tractor-Trailer for commercial purpose.

Therefore,
based on these grounds, the Commissioner has fastened the liability on the owner of the Tractor-Trailer.

7. Admittedly, insurance policy issued is for agriculture purpose but the owner himself had stated while giving statement before the police that he has given his Tractor- Trailer to one contractor K.S.Raju on hire basis for carrying out PWD works.
The said contractor K.S.Raju had stated in the complaint before the police that he has taken the Tractor- Trailer on hire basis from the respondent No.1 for carrying out PWD work.
Therefore, these evidence produced before the learned Commissioner proves that the contractor had used the Tractor-Trailer for PWD work, which amounts to violation of condition of policy.
Therefore, learned Commissioner is correct in holding that there is violation of condition of policy and accordingly, fastened liability on the owner of the Tractor- Trailer.
Hence, this finding of learned Commissioner is correct which needs no interference by this Court.
NC: 2023:KHC:24855 8. QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:-
The claimant was working as a Coolie under the employment of the respondent No.1.
The learned Commissioner has committed an error in holding monthly wage of the claimant at Rs.1,850/-.
But as per Section 4 of the WC Act, monthly wage is considered as Rs.4,000/-.
The doctor opined that claimant has suffered 15 to 20% of disability to whole body.
Accordingly, learned Commissioner is correct in holding 20% disability towards whole body.
The claimant was aged about 22 years.

Therefore,
the relevant factor applicable is 221.37.

Hence, the loss of earning capacity due to disability is re-assessed and quantified as Rs.4,000 x 60% x 20% x 221.37 =
1,06,257/-.

Accordingly, a sum of Rs.1,06,257/- is awarded under the head 'loss of earning capacity due to disability'.
9.
The Labour Court has awarded the compensation of Rs.49,144/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,06,257/-.
Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.57,113/- (Rs.1,06,257- Rs.49,144).

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

Sri Nagaraj vs Ninge Gowda on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171243086/
3 ii.

The judgment and award passed by the Labour Officer and Commissioner for the W o r k m e n C o m p e n s a t i o n , D i v i s i o n - 2 , C h i k m a g a l u r , i n c a s e No.WCA/NF.No.91/2002 dated 10.01.2012 is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.57,113/- with interest @ 12% p.a., from the date of accident till its realization.
iii. The respondent No.1 - owner of the Tractor-Trailer is directed to pay the above said compensation to the appellant/claimant.
iv. The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 111 days in filing the appeal.
v. Costs made easy.

vi. Ordered accordingly.
